title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
snippet: Domestic violence includes physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, and economic abuse in a shared household; aggrieved persons can seek reliefs under the Act.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
snippet: Magistrates may pass protection, residence, monetary relief, custody, and compensation orders; breach of protection orders is punishable.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
snippet: An application can be filed before the Magistrate by the aggrieved person or a protection officer; interim and ex parte orders are available in urgent situations.

title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
snippet: Employers must constitute an Internal Committee and display the penal consequences of sexual harassment; inquiries must be completed within a time-bound manner with confidentiality.

title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
snippet: During inquiry the ICC may recommend transfer, leave, or restraint on the respondent; malicious false complaints may attract action as prescribed.

title: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
snippet: Giving, taking, or abetting dowry is an offence; demanding dowry directly or indirectly is punishable with imprisonment and fine.

title: Indian Penal Code, 1860
snippet: Cruelty or harassment of a woman by her husband or relatives for dowry or otherwise is a cognizable offence; FIR can be registered on credible information.

title: Indian Penal Code, 1860
snippet: Assault or criminal force to outrage modesty, sexual harassment, stalking, and voyeurism are specific offences with punishments; police investigate as per procedure.

title: Indian Penal Code, 1860
snippet: Rape and aggravated rape are serious offences with stringent punishment; medical examination, consent, and survivor rights follow BNSS and allied rules.

title: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
snippet: Offences against SC/ST women including atrocities and humiliation attract special procedures, mandatory registration, and fast-track trial provisions.

title: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
snippet: Child marriages are voidable; child marriage prohibition officers and courts can issue injunctions; adult males contracting child marriage commit an offence.

title: Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986
snippet: Advertisement or publication that indecently depicts women in violation of the Act is prohibited and punishable.

title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971
snippet: Termination within prescribed gestational limits and conditions must be by registered medical practitioners at approved facilities; beyond limits special boards apply under amended law.

title: Family Courts Act, 1984
snippet: Family Courts hear matrimonial disputes, maintenance, and custody with a duty to assist settlement; procedures are simpler and child welfare is paramount in custody matters.

title: Anonymized PWDVA protection · Pune district
section: Illustrative outcome: interim protection and residence order
snippet: Anonymized legal-aid style notes from Pune district: a woman filed under the Domestic Violence Act with medical papers, a short incident diary, and two witnesses; the Magistrate passed interim protection and residence orders and listed counselling. This is a training pattern, not a cited judgment.
documents_used: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship

title: Anonymized PWDVA application · Pune district
snippet: Anonymized pattern from Pune district: an application was filed months after leaving the shared household with almost no documentary proof and reluctant witnesses; interim orders were narrow and enforcement was difficult. Early documentation and local support help. Illustrative only.

title: Anonymized POSH inquiry · Chennai district
section: Illustrative outcome: employer action on IC recommendations
snippet: Anonymized outreach example in Chennai: an employee submitted a written complaint to the Internal Committee with email trails; the IC inquired and recommended shifting the respondent and counselling; implementation varied by employer. Not a published case; every workplace differs.
